 Cavaliers vs. Timberwolves Prediction: Preview, Injury Report, Advantages, And X-Factors
 The Cleveland Cavaliers host the Minnesota Timberwolves at Rocket Arena on Monday, October 26, at 7:00 PM ET.
 Fran Leiva 
 Oct 26, 2026 
 9 Min Read 
 Share 
 Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images 
 The Minnesota Timberwolves have been destroying teams to start the season, and now they’re taking their perfect 3-0 record to Rocket Arena to face the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday, October 26, at 7:00 PM ET.
 Cleveland is 1-1, including a 1-0 home record, while Minnesota has already won twice on the road. And after watching these first few games, I’m really curious to see if the Cavaliers can finally make the Timberwolves work for a win.
 Cleveland almost blew another massive lead on Saturday, but managed to escape with a 125-121 victory over the Nets. Donovan Mitchell scored 22 points, while Jarrett Allen added 21. Mitchell is putting up 27.0 points, 7.5 rebounds, and 3.5 assists through two games, with Evan Mobley contributing 19.0 points, 9.0 rebounds, and 3.0 assists.
 Minnesota hasn’t had any of those problems. The Timberwolves just beat the Raptors 117-94, with Anthony Edwards scoring 26 points and Rudy Gobert grabbing 13 rebounds. Edwards is already producing 28.7 points, 5.0 rebounds, and 3.3 assists per game, while LaMelo Ball has added 16.5 points and 5.5 assists.
 And here’s something pretty insane: Minnesota has won all three games by at least 20 points, becoming just the third team in NBA history to start a season that way. The Cavaliers split their two meetings with the Timberwolves last season, winning the most recent one 146-134, but this Minnesota team looks pretty scary right now.
 Injury Report 
 Cavaliers 
 Nae’Qwan Tomlin: Out (left low back stress reaction)
 Khalifa Diop: Out (left knee injury management)
 Timberwolves 
 Anthony Edwards: Questionable (left knee injury management)
 Donte DiVincenzo: Out (right Achilles tendon surgery recovery)
 Why The Cavaliers Have The Advantage 
 I don’t think Cleveland has played particularly well yet, but the offensive talent is obviously there. The Cavaliers scored 69 points in the first half against the 76ers before somehow throwing away a 29-point lead, then followed that up by shooting 50.6% from the field against Brooklyn.
 And with Mitchell, James Harden , Mobley, and Allen sharing the floor, there aren’t many easy defensive assignments for Minnesota. Mitchell is already scoring 27.0 points per game, while Mobley and Allen are combining for 36.5 points and 16.5 rebounds. That’s quite a bit of production coming from the frontcourt alone.
 Allen was especially good against the Nets, finishing with 21 points on 7-of-8 shooting. Mobley added 20 points, 10 rebounds, and three blocks, and the two combined to miss just five shots. Now, doing that against Gobert and Minnesota’s defense will obviously be much harder, but Cleveland has enough size to make this a proper battle inside.
 Another thing I like is the possibility of forcing Gobert into defending more pick-and-rolls. Harden and Mitchell can both attack those situations, and if Cleveland manages to get Gobert away from the basket, Mobley and Allen should have more room to finish.
 But man, those turnovers need to stop. The Cavaliers are giving the ball away 22.0 times per game, which is honestly ridiculous for a team with two experienced guards controlling the offense. They already wasted a 29-point lead against Philadelphia and nearly lost another 22-point advantage against Brooklyn.
 Do that against Minnesota, and there’s a pretty good chance you’re losing by double digits before the fourth quarter.
 Why The Timberwolves Have The Advantage 
 Three games, three wins, and not a single opponent has even come close to reaching 110 points. That’s how Minnesota has opened its season, beating the Heat by 25, the Magic by 22, and the Raptors by 23.
 The Timberwolves are scoring 121.0 points per game while allowing just 97.7, and their shooting has been absolutely ridiculous. They’re making 16.7 threes per contest on 42.4% shooting, while Cleveland is hitting just 11.5 on 34.3%.
 And I think the arrival of Ball has made a pretty obvious difference. Edwards can still take over whenever he wants, but he doesn’t need to handle every possession anymore. Minnesota has another guard who can find shooters, create opportunities in transition, and make defenses pay for focusing too much on Ant.
 The defensive side might be even crazier. Minnesota has a 95.1 defensive rating and is grabbing 54.0 rebounds per game, with Gobert controlling the paint and Jaden McDaniels making life miserable for opposing wings.
 Just look at what happened against Toronto. Scottie Barnes went scoreless on 0-of-12 shooting, Jakob Poeltl finished with zero points and one rebound, and the Raptors barely reached 94 points.
 Now imagine that defense facing a Cavaliers team that’s already committing 22.0 turnovers per game. Edwards, McDaniels, and the rest of the perimeter defenders can turn careless passes into easy points. And considering Cleveland has already struggled to protect huge leads, I wouldn’t be surprised if Minnesota gets another opportunity to completely take over a game after halftime.
 X-Factors 
 I’m still waiting for James Harden to have a proper offensive game with the Cavaliers this season. He’s putting up 14.0 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 6.0 assists, but he’s made only six of his first 20 field-goal attempts. Against Brooklyn, he finished with 12 points despite going 1-of-8 from the field. Cleveland needs more scoring from him, especially with McDaniels likely spending plenty of time guarding Mitchell.
 Jarrett Allen also has a pretty important matchup against Gobert. His 21 points against the Nets were excellent, but the Cavaliers need him to compete on the glass after Minnesota grabbed 54.0 rebounds per game through its first three appearances. If Gobert starts collecting offensive rebounds and creating second chances, things could get ugly for Cleveland pretty quickly.
 For Minnesota, I really want to see what LaMelo Ball does against Harden. He scored 15 points and delivered eight assists in just 17 minutes against Toronto, shooting 4-of-5 from three before foul trouble limited his playing time. Cleveland hasn’t been particularly impressive defending opposing guards, so Ball should have plenty of opportunities to attack.
 And don’t forget about Jaden McDaniels, who had 14 points, six rebounds, and three blocks against the Raptors. He’ll probably get the Mitchell assignment for most of the night, and that’s going to be one of my favorite matchups to watch. Mitchell can still score against anybody, but McDaniels has the length to make those pull-up jumpers and drives much more difficult.
 Prediction 
 I actually think Cleveland will give Minnesota its toughest game of the season so far. Mitchell is looking good offensively, Mobley and Allen have been efficient, and the Cavaliers finally get to play a team coming off a game the previous night.
 But I’m having a hard time picking against Minnesota right now. The Timberwolves are shooting 42.4% from three, allowing fewer than 98 points per game, and winning by an average of 23.3 points. Meanwhile, Cleveland has already blown one massive lead and nearly wasted another.
 I expect Mitchell to score plenty and keep the Cavaliers competitive, but Edwards and Ball should have enough offense to finish the job. And with Gobert and McDaniels defending the basket and perimeter, I trust Minnesota to get the stops when the game gets close.
 Prediction: Timberwolves 117, Cavaliers 112
